grammar.label: the obituary, the citation and the tribute
grammar.form: the claim to significance first; the chronology; the qualification that humanises
grammar.meaning: records a life or an achievement in the shape the genre requires

explanation.en: An obituary opens with why this life is being recorded, not with a birth date. The best ones include the failure or the difficulty, because a subject with no shadow is not a person. The genre rewards specificity over praise: one exact detail outweighs a paragraph of admiration.
explanation.uz: Nekrolog tug'ilgan sana bilan emas, nima uchun bu hayot yozilayotgani bilan boshlanadi. Eng yaxshilarida qiyinchilik ham bor, chunki soyasiz odam — odam emas.

grammar.positive_example: She was the first woman to hold the post and she held it for nineteen difficult years.
grammar.negative_example: She was born in 1946 and had a long and distinguished career in public service.

l1_notes.uz: Nekrolog janri ingliz matbuotida aniq shaklga ega; o'zbek an'anasida boshqacha.

grammar.label: the speech — written to be heard once
grammar.form: short clauses; repeated frames; signposting; no subordination the ear cannot hold
grammar.meaning: carries an argument to a listener who cannot re-read

explanation.en: A listener has no second chance, so the sentence that works on the page may fail in the hall. Speech grammar front-loads the point, repeats the frame, and avoids the long subordinate opening that a reader would simply hold in mind. A speech that reads well often sounds bad, and the reverse.
explanation.uz: Tinglovchida ikkinchi imkoniyat yo'q. Nutq grammatikasi fikrni oldinga qo'yadi, ramkani takrorlaydi va uzun ergash gap bilan boshlamaydi.

grammar.positive_example: We have three problems. The first is money. I will come back to the other two.
grammar.negative_example: Because of the funding difficulties that arose after the second inspection, we have problems.

l1_notes.uz: Yozma va og'zaki nutq grammatikasi ingliz tilida sezilarli farq qiladi.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Four minutes. They gave me six.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Take the four. Read me the opening.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Mr Karimov ran this office for nineteen years. Nineteen difficult years, and he never once sent out a report that he had not read to the end.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: You have not said anywhere that he was a great man.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have said what he did. The room can do the rest.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is the whole craft. A tribute that praises directly begins to sound like a letter of reference.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is a line I am not sure about. 'He was not easy to work for.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Keep it. Every person in that room knows it, and a tribute that leaves it out is about somebody else.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is written to be heard once.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: So read it aloud now, and cut anything your own mouth stumbles on. The ear is given no second chance.
